subject: Sizing discussion: Dedicated vs Private for Acme regulated workloads
messages:
From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acmecorp.com>, Linda Zhao <linda.zhao@acmecorp.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sizing for Dedicated vs Private for Acme regulated workloads

Hi Sanjay / Linda,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our call, I attached a first-pass capacity proposal (capacity_proposal_v2.xlsx) and a high-level VPC diagram (network_diagram_vpc.pdf). This note summarizes the assumptions we used and two deployment paths to compare: Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools in our hosted infra but customer-isolated tenancy) vs Redwood Private (customer-managed VPC / on-prem package).

Key assumptions (please confirm):
- Steady-state concurrency: 120 sustained concurrent chat sessions (95th pct traffic)
- Peak burst concurrency: 450 concurrent sessions (short spikes, ~10 min)
- Average sequence length: 800 tokens (prompt + response)
- Throughput requirement: 18 tokens/sec per session on average => ~2160 tokens/sec sustained
- Latency SLO (p95): sub-400ms for 256-token responses, fallback to smaller model for larger responses
- Model family: enterprise-optimized redwood-2 variants (quantized) for safety/regulation tests

Prelim capacity mapping (high level):
- Dedicated: 6 H100-backed workers (4 shards), continuous batching + KV cache gives target cost/latency sweet spot for the above workload. Supports region failover and reserved throughput.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): recommended 8 x A100-80GB equivalent nodes (or 6 x H100 depending on availability) due to lack of shared multi-tenant blocking and added headroom for batch windows/evictions.

Tradeoffs:
- Isolation: Private gives full network isolation and on-prem control (preferred for regulated PII workflows). Dedicated can provide tenant isolation + SOC2 controls but requires VPC peering and stricter egress controls.
- Cost: Dedicated will usually be lower TCO when usage is high because we amortize clustering. Private has higher fixed infra and ops overhead but maximum control.
- Ops / SLAs: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed latency/uptime and Redwood-managed updates. Private requires co-managed upgrade plans and optional support add-on.

Next asks: can you confirm the steady-state concurrency & peak windows above, retention/observability window for audit logs (days), and whether KMS/HSM integration is required end-to-end? Once confirmed we’ll finalize the numeric sizing and a procurement-ready quote.

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm assumptions (concurrency, retention, KMS).
2) We’ll produce a 2-page executive comparison + cost run for Dedicated vs Private (by 3/10).
3) Schedule a short network workshop with your infra team (30–45m) to validate VPC/e2e controls.

Thanks,
Dev
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0132

Attachment stubs: capacity_proposal_v2.xlsx (worksheet: sizing), network_diagram_vpc.pdf
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acmecorp.com>

Cc: Linda Zhao <linda.zhao@acmecorp.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing for Dedicated vs Private for Acme regulated workloads

Thanks Dev — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Isolation/regulation: our primary workloads will touch regulated customer PII. Our security team requires that data remains inside our VPC or on-prem; we are skeptical of multi-tenant hosting even with SOC2 unless we can have VPC peering and customer-managed keys.
2) Concurrency numbers: the steady-state figure (~120) looks right; peak windows could be larger if a bulk reporting job fires (~600 for 5–10 minutes).
3) KMS: yes — customer-managed keys are mandatory for encryption at rest for models/prefix cache.
4) Audit logs: we need 365 days of searchable audit logs; storage can be cold but must be retrievable for e-discovery.

Given (1) and (3), Private deployment seems to be the safer procurement route for now. That said, if you can outline a Dedicated configuration that satisfies VPC peering + bring-your-own-KMS + 365-day logs, please call that out explicitly in the quote — we’ll evaluate both from a TCO and legal-risk angle.

Also: procurement timeline — we are planning procurement signoff by end of Q2, but legal/security approvals are gating.

Sanjay Rao
VP Product Ops | Acme Corp
sanjay@acmecorp.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acmecorp.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>, rachel_kim <rachel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 08:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing for Dedicated vs Private for Acme regulated workloads

Sanjay — appreciate the precision. I sketched a slightly more actionable sizing & rollout plan based on the clarified peaks and audit window. See inline bullets.

Minimum Private footprint (for on-prem or VPC-hosted customer-managed infra):
- 8 x A100-80GB (or 6 x H100-80GB) nodes for model serving (primary cluster)
- 2 x spare nodes for rolling upgrades / failover
- 4 x control-plane instances (small VMs) for telemetry, batching coordinator, and KV-store (replicated)
- Storage for 365-day audit logs: estimate ~12 TB cold storage initially (S3 Glacier / object store) + 1 TB hot index for search

Recommended Dedicated footprint (Redwood-managed, tenant-isolated):
- Reserved pool: 6 x H100-equivalent workers in US-west with automated autoscale buffer to handle 600 concurrent short spikes via burst pools
- Encryption: BYOK via KMS integration + encrypted snapshots. We can accept customer KMS for data-at-rest keys and integrate with your HSM if required (we will need an onboarding security exercise).
- Logs: 365-day retention available as a paid add-on; storage lives in your dedicated tenant project and is exportable to your S3 bucket nightly.

Rollout proposal (high-level):
1) Network workshop (30–45m) to validate VPC peering and routing (deliverable: network checklist).
2) Pilot (2 weeks): 2-node private cluster or 3-worker dedicated pool with synthetic load & audit review.
3) Canary & ramp (4 weeks): increase to steady-state, test failover, validate KMS and e-discovery flows.

Open questions for our infra team (cc Marcus to answer):
- Marcus: can you confirm whether Dedicated supports direct customer KMS integration for snapshot encryption today, or if we need the on-prem HSM path?
- Marcus: what's the expected lead time for shipping H100 reserved capacity if Acme signs a Dedicated contract (we want a queue/ETA).

—Laura
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acmecorp.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev@redwood.com>
Cc: rachel_kim <rachel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing for Dedicated vs Private for Acme regulated workloads

Thanks — quick answers from infra: 

- KMS/BYOK: Dedicated supports BYOK integration with major cloud KMS providers today (Google KMS / AWS KMS). For HSM-backed keys we have a narrow integration path (requires additional security review) but it's feasible.
- Logs retention: we can enable 365-day retention as an add-on for Dedicated; logs are stored in a tenant-bucket and can be exported to your S3 nightly. Search indexing costs are separate; we gave a conservative estimate in the attached workbook.
- H100 lead time: depends on region capacity but conservative procurement lead-time for reserved H100 is ~6–10 weeks to provision dedicated reserved pool. We can discuss temporary burst capacity on our hosted fleet while physical workers are queued.

Sizing comment: given the 600-concurrent short spikes, you'll want a dedicated burst pool (either Dedicated reserved burst + autoscale) or run Private with extra headroom. Private will require more upfront nodes to avoid queueing during the 5–10 minute peaks.

I'll prepare an appendix to the workbook with two concrete node-count scenarios (Private vs Dedicated) and cost delta assuming a 12-month commitment. Expect that by tomorrow EOD.

-Marcus
Director, Inference Infrastructure | Redwood Inference

Dev/Laura — procurement here. We reviewed the proposal briefly and attached a preliminary PO (po_acme_031026.pdf) as a placeholder so legal can see figures while security completes the review. A few procurement notes: 

- Procurement prefers Dedicated if the legal team is comfortable with our KMS and VPC peering controls. Please include a line item for the 365-day log retention addon and the BYOK integration effort (one-time setup fee), plus estimated timeline for H100 provisioning if we go Dedicated.
- If we proceed with Private, include an ops support SLA (24x7 support) optional line.
- Please provide a DocuSign-ready quote (we need costs rolled up for both Dedicated and Private options).

We are targeting an internal go/no-go on provider choice by 2026-06-30.

Thanks,
Linda Zhao
Sr. Procurement Manager | Acme Corp
